title: Machine learning exposed a structure in terminal-singularity classification
summary: A neural-network classifier trained on eight-dimensional, Picard-rank-two toric varieties achieved 95% accuracy on a five-million-example test set and enabled rapid generation of a much larger predicted landscape of Q-Fano varieties. The authors report that the model’s classification pattern led them to formulate a new combinatorial criterion for terminal singularities, which they prove mathematically. The learned model suggested the route to the theorem; it did not supply the proof.
ai_technology: Feed-forward neural-network classifier trained on toric-variety weight matrices
organization: Imperial College London; University of Nottingham

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 metadata and full text for posting date, author affiliations, learned-classifier results and connection to the stated mathematical criterion; linked NeurIPS proceedings identity checked.

evidence.tested: The authors report a 95% classification accuracy on a balanced test split of five million eight-dimensional toric-variety examples and use the model to explore a larger Q-Fano landscape. They formulate and prove a new combinatorial criterion for terminal singularities, motivated by the ML analysis.
evidence.unknown: The 95% is internal held-out classification performance, not independent external validation; the authors state the neural network does not itself perform the theorem’s divisibility-based test or proof.
evidence.ai_role: The trained neural-network classifier revealed a tractable pattern in the classification landscape and directly motivated the authors’ new combinatorial criterion; the authors separately establish its correctness by proof.
